title: Pacing-Walk
primitive: where the tale walks fast, where it walks slow, and why each pace lets a different thing land
summary: A told tale is a walk. The teller decides where to RUN past the trees and where to STOP at one tree. This kit listens for the pace inside each beat — the Hook can sprint, the Turn often slows, the Close can either rush or hold. Phase 2 makes pace a craft choice instead of an accident.

questions.prompt: Tell a 60-second tale and pay attention to where you RUSHED and where you HELD. Was the rushing on purpose? Was the holding on purpose? What would change if you swapped them?
Which beat is usually the strongest place to SLOW the pace and add one small specific detail?
options: The Hook — the listener arrives, so detail anchors them.
The Turn — the listener is meeting the meaning, so a held moment makes the meaning land.
The Close — the listener is leaving, so detail helps the goodbye.
questions.rationale: The Turn rotates the meaning. Slowing it down with one specific image lets the rotation arrive instead of zipping past. Hook detail is good but can be carried by voice; Close detail is good but a quick close also works.

questions.prompt: Find a tale in your anthology that felt too fast. Which beat was the fast one? Pick the moment you'd slow if you re-told it tomorrow. Name the one detail you'd add.

Take a tale that rushed past the Turn. Rewrite ONE sentence at the Turn — make it hold for one extra breath. Add one specific image (a smell, a temperature, a small movement). Read both versions aloud.

castCameos.line: Slowing is a gift. The held moment is where the listener notices what THEY brought to the tale — that's where the tale becomes ours, not just yours.
When the teller slows on purpose, I lean in. When they slow by accident, I check my watch. The difference is whether the pause has a SHAPE.
Pace changes ARE pivots. Sprinting the rising action and slowing the Turn is one of the oldest moves — the contrast IS the rotation.
Try a slow-fast-slow rhythm: held Hook → rushing Setup + Rising → held Turn → quick Close. The Hook and the Turn echo each other. Listeners feel the symmetry.
